subject: Surge commit and tier-skip transition
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sam Walker <sam@keyloom.io>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Surge commit and tier-skip transition

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Per our conversation, Keyloom is seeing a predictable surge pattern through Q3 and wants to lock in higher committed capacity with the Hosted API to avoid throttles and keep unit costs stable.

Primary ask: increase monthly commit from 1.2B tokens to 3.5B tokens starting Sept 1, with a one-month ramp (50% Sept / 75% Oct / 100% Nov). You mentioned wanting to skip the intermediate "mid" tier if we can offer a temporary concession on rate bands while capacity is reserved — that aligns with a short-term tier-skip.

Attached is an initial quote and a draft SOW for the uplift and operational onboarding. Key items I'd like to confirm before I loop in Finance/Legal/Provisioning:
- Target monthly commit and ramp schedule (above)
- Preferred term length (12 vs 24 months) — you said you lean 12 but willing to discuss
- SLA expectations and soft-throttle grace window during burst events
- Procurement timeline for PO/DocuSign

If that matches your expectations, can we schedule a 30-min call early next week to finalize rates and DocuSign? I can invite Karthik (pricing) and Lauren (ops/implementation) to join.

Thanks,

Rafael
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Keyloom_Surge_Quote_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: Keyloom_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sam Walker <sam@keyloom.io>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@keyloom.io
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surge commit and tier-skip transition

Rafael —

Appreciate the summary and the docs. High level, that plan looks workable. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock term length: 

1) Can you confirm the effective per-token rate at 3.5B vs current 1.2B? We need the unit economics to line up with our forecast.
2) What does "temporary concession on rate bands" look like in practice? We want a clear end date and a hard cap on overage exposure.
3) Ops question: will burst pockets be pre-provisioned or on-demand? We prefer pre-provisioned capacity to avoid cold-start throttles.

We have procurement in copy — they typically need a filled questionnaire and draft PO terms. Attaching procurement questionnaire for you to populate if helpful. Also happy to do the 30-min call next Tue AM (our timezone Pacific).

Sam
Director, Platform Engineering
Keyloom Labs
[Attachment: procurement_questionnaire_filled.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Surge commit and tier-skip transition (Keyloom) — pricing + provisioning ask

Folks — forwarding Sam's reply and attached procurement questionnaire. TL;DR: Keyloom wants to move from 1.2B -> 3.5B monthly commit starting Sept with a documented ramp, wants to skip the mid-tier for one quarter if we can provide a capped concession on rate bands and pre-provision burst pockets.

Questions for pricing/ops: 
- Karthik: can you provide a per-token blended rate for 3.5B commit (12-mo and 24-mo) and a template for a "temporary concession" (explicit end date + max overage exposure)? Also flag any discount thresholds we should call out.
- Lauren/Monica: what is the operational lead time to pre-provision burst pockets aligned with Sept 1 start? Any gating items (VPC peering, ACLs, provisioning windows)?

Sam is available Tue AM PT for a 30-min sync. I propose we prepare a one-pager with: committed rates, concession mechanics, provisioning checklist, and a DocuSign-ready Term Sheet.

I'll coordinate internal prep and bring the one-pager to the call.

Thanks,
Rafael

> > Rafael —
> > 
> > Appreciate the summary and the docs. High level, that plan looks workable...

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sam Walker <sam@keyloom.io>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@keyloom.io
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Surge commit and tier-skip transition — proposal and next steps

Sam / Keyloom team —

Thanks for the quick reply and for the completed questionnaire. Per Rafael's note, we've put together a short proposal and the operational checklist you requested. Summary highlights below and the full quote is attached.

Proposal highlights (12-month term)
- Commit: 3.5B tokens / month, start date 2026-09-01
- Ramp: 50% Sept (1.75B), 75% Oct (2.625B), 100% Nov (3.5B)
- Rate: $0.0000125 per token on committed usage (blended)
- Temporary concession: For months Sept-Nov we will honor an intermediate rate band for committed volume equal to 90% of the standard mid-tier rate; concession ends 2026-11-30. Overages beyond committed levels billed at standard overage rate; maximum monthly overage exposure capped at 10% of committed spend for the concession window.
- Burst pockets: Pre-provisioned burst capacity (50% of committed baseline) available via provisioning ticket; activation guaranteed within 4 hours of request during business hours.

Operational next steps
1) Review attached Term Sheet and SOW; sign via DocuSign link below to lock the Sept 1 start date.
2) Procurement: please issue PO referencing deal KL-2026-Q3-42 once DocuSign completes.
3) Network & Provisioning: Monica will reach out to confirm VPC/peering details and schedule provisioning window (target 8/24 — 8/28).

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/0a1b2c3d4e5f
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/KL-2026-Q3-42

Attachments: Keyloom_Surge_Quote_v1.xlsx, Keyloom_SOW_v2.pdf

If that works, Rafael — can you confirm the Tue morning sync at 9:00 AM PT? We'll bring the term sheet and a short slide with provisioning milestones.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
